description.narrative: 1.0 Improved livelihoods and resilience of subsistence farmers through reforestation and building the carbon store locked up for economic return

title.narrative: 1.0a Percentage of target population (Suco level) that have improved livelihoods (especially diversication and income) through reforestation and / or building the carbon store for economic return.

description.narrative: 1.0a Percentage of target population (Suco level) that have improved livelihoods (especially diversication and income) through reforestation and / or building the carbon store for economic return.

comment.narrative: Baseline survey has not yet been finalised and this data will be updated once completed

Just 26 of respondents had cash savings demonstrating that the Action is working in vulnerable communities while 28 of those who had received payments from credits from reforestation had cash savings while all respondents who said a member of their household belong to a village savings and loans community savings group also had cash savings. This demonstrates the extent to which these two initiatives help strengthen resilience and livelihoods among target communities. The proportion of respondents who had a corrugated iron or concrete roof was lower for those who had received payments for carbon reforestation than respondents overall at 55 compared to 63 while those whose house had a concrete floor was also lower at 34 compared to 44. In response to the question do the household members own animals 96 said yes while for those who had had payments for reforestation carbon credits all households said yes. These results show that the Action is having a beneficial impact on target communities in terms of prevalence of savings as well as marginally higher number of animals but the differences were marginal overall and this can be attributed to delays in the Action being implemented and we anticipate by project completion there will be more noticeable impact.

title.narrative: 1.0 Improved livelihoods and resilience of subsistence farmers through reforestation and building the carbon store locked up for economic return

description.narrative: 1.0 Improved livelihoods and resilience of subsistence farmers through reforestation and building the carbon store locked up for economic return

title.narrative: 1.0b Percentage of target population (suco) that have improved resilience through reforestation and / or building the carbon store for economic return.

description.narrative: 1.0b Percentage of target population (suco) that have improved resilience through reforestation and / or building the carbon store for economic return.

comment.narrative: Baseline survey is currently being completed indicator data will be updated once report is finalised

Results taken from baseline survey which compares baseline and endline to see improvements over time. As such final values will be provided at the endline stage. However as will be provided in the annual report from the baseline analysis some context is provided belowRespondents who had received payments for carbon reforestation were more likely to be confident or very confident they could recover from an environmental shock or agricultural impact without external support at 77 compared to 73 overall. In addition respondents who had received payments from carbon credits were also more likely to have more than six months worth of food stored than respondents overall at 47 compared to 41. There was not a difference between those who had received payments for carbon reforestation compared to those who had not in terms of having more than the amount of food stored generally at this time of year. Respondents who had received payments for carbon reforestation were more likely to say they felt confident they could recover from a family shock without external support at 79 compared to 63 while they were also marginally more likely 71 compared to 70 to say they were confident or very confident recovering from an economic shock without external support. In terms of income the average income level was higher for all respondents compared to those who had received reforestation carbon credits and those who belonged to savings and loans groups. It was notable that some respondents had significantly higher incomes than anticipated that may have impacted the results.
